Europe Under-20 Championship|2017 Greece]]|[[France national basketball team|National team]]}} }} '''Élie-Franck Okobo''' (born 23 October 1997) is a French professional [[basketball]] player for [[Dubai Basketball]] of the [[ABA League]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. A {{height|ft=6|in=3}} tall [[combo guard]], the [[Bordeaux]] native began his club career at age 16. Okobo subsequently competed for the [[reserve team|youth team]] of [[Élan Béarnais|Élan Béarnais Pau-Lacq-Orthez]], reaching the [[:fr:Championnat de France de basket-ball Espoirs|LNB Espoirs]] title game in 2016. In the [[2016–17 Pro A season|2016–17 season]], he assumed a greater role with the senior team, and in the following year, he became a regular starter. Okobo has represented France at international competition on multiple occasions. He was a key player for the under-20 team at the [[FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], which he took part in twice, winning a bronze medal in [[2017 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship|2017]]. Okobo has also suited up for the [[France national basketball team|senior national team]] at [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe)|FIBA World Cup qualification]]. He has been considered one of the top international prospects, and at one point was considered a potential first-round selection, for the [[2018 NBA draft]]. However, he was taken as the 31st overall pick in the second round by the [[Phoenix Suns]] that year. ==Early life and career== Okobo was born in [[Bordeaux]], France to a Congolese father and French mother.{{cite web|title=Did Sean Marks divert his plane to France for a look at Elie Okobo?|url=https://www.netsdaily.com/2018/3/18/17135986/did-sean-marks-divert-his-plane-to-france-for-a-look-at-elie-okobo|publisher=Nets Daily|access-date=April 12, 2018|date=March 18, 2018|archive-date=April 13, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413125606/https://www.netsdaily.com/2018/3/18/17135986/did-sean-marks-divert-his-plane-to-france-for-a-look-at-elie-okobo|url-status=live}}{{cite AV media|people=Okobo, Elie|date=January 20, 2018|title=Elie Okobo Interview|medium=Video|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PEgqK_h2FLY|location=[[Pau, Pyrénées-Atlantiques|Pau]]|publisher=DraftExpress}} He has one sister and two brothers: his older brother plays [[handball]] and competes in [[track and field]], while his younger brother also plays basketball. In addition, Okobo's father has basketball experience as well.
